cohort: 13,432 childbearing women aged 15-49 years assisted in 66 maternity hospitals of the Unified Health System (SUS) and private associated facilities in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from September 2017 to October 2019
finding: Despite almost universal prenatal care coverage, only half of the participants received adequate prenatal care, defined as care initiated by the 12th gestational week with at least 6 appointments.
mod_finding: Among women who had a vaginal delivery, older age, white race, higher education level, fewer previous deliveries, and residence in the Valleys macro-region were associated with increased likelihood of adequate prenatal care.
